title: Public dense QQ right kernel
objective: Route public dense QQ right_kernel through the generated one-elimination FLINT resource with canonical semantics, no packed materialization, and a measured performance gate

handoff.summary: Routes public dense QQ right_kernel() and right_kernel_matrix() through the generated one-elimination FmpqMatrix resource operation on Node. The result remains a canonically reduced, immutable, independently owned rational matrix resource; rank and kernel caches preserve Sage semantics. The packed typed-Python implementation remains the portable capability fallback. Focused tests prohibit rational N-API and packed materialization, cover native-disabled execution, randomized rectangular and degenerate matrices, 4097-bit coefficient skew, mutation invalidation, cache identity, and independent RREF verification. The quiet-host rational matrix gate measures the public 60x90 right kernel at 13.40 ms, essentially the cost of its single 13.53 ms RREF and well below the new 35 ms budget.
risks: Generated FmpqMatrix resources remain declared wasm=false. Browser and other portable targets continue through the existing tested packed typed-Python fallback, so this lane does not yet prove opaque-resource WebAssembly lowering.

The public route depends on the generated fmpq_matrix_right_kernel operation and its sanitizer-backed lifecycle tests from the shared base; this lane adds public ownership, cache, and no-materialization coverage rather than duplicating the low-level sanitizer harness.
next_steps: Prove generated FmpqMatrix resource lowering on WebAssembly while retaining the same public Matrix API and portable packed semantics.
After integration, consider adding an explicit left-kernel performance case; left_kernel() already reaches this resource route through transpose().right_kernel().
Continue routing remaining public dense QQ algorithms through generated resource operations without packed compatibility materialization.
